skill.name: benchling-integration
skill.description: Benchling integration guidance for registry, inventory, ELN, workflow, API, SDK, and Data Warehouse automation.
skill.summary: Use Benchling APIs and SDK patterns to automate lab data workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The static analyzer flagged 143 patterns, but the reviewed content is documentation for expected Benchling API usage. The findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, placeholder URLs, placeholder credentials, environment variable examples, and local CSV examples. No prompt injection, hidden execution, unauthorized exfiltration, or malicious intent was found in the scanned files.

remediation.issue: Some examples show placeholder API keys directly inside constructors.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer environment-variable examples in the main guide and keep inline placeholders clearly marked as non-secret sample values.

remediation.issue: Many documentation examples look executable to static scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Label examples as illustrative and add a short note that users must review tenant URLs, permissions, and exported data paths before running them.

content.value_statement: Life science teams need consistent ways to connect Benchling data with lab and analytics workflows. This skill provides practical SDK, API, authentication, and automation guidance for Benchling integrations.
actual_capabilities: Explains Benchling API key, OAuth, and OIDC authentication patterns.
Provides SDK examples for registry entities, inventory, ELN entries, and workflows.
Documents REST endpoint patterns, headers, pagination, and error handling.
Outlines event integration with AWS EventBridge and downstream systems.
Describes Data Warehouse access for analytics and reporting workflows.
limitations: It does not include a packaged executable connector or live API client.
Users must provide their own Benchling tenant, credentials, and permissions.
Examples use placeholder IDs and must be adapted to each tenant schema.
It does not validate compliance, retention, or lab governance requirements.

use_cases.title: Build registry automation
use_cases.description: Create and update DNA, RNA, protein, and custom entities with consistent SDK patterns.

use_cases.title: Coordinate inventory workflows
use_cases.description: Model samples, containers, locations, transfers, and workflow tasks for daily lab operations.

use_cases.title: Prepare analytics pipelines
use_cases.description: Plan exports, Data Warehouse queries, and event-driven syncs for reporting systems.

prompt_templates.title: Set up Benchling access
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new tenant connection.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me set up a Benchling SDK connection using environment variables. Include required tenant URL, credential choices, and a safe test request.

prompt_templates.title: Create registry entities
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a Benchling workflow to create DNA sequences, set schema fields, register them, and handle pagination for later review.

prompt_templates.title: Automate inventory and ELN links
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Benchling automation that creates containers, transfers samples, creates an ELN entry, and links the related registry entities.

prompt_templates.title: Plan enterprise integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a secure Benchling integration using OAuth, EventBridge events, Data Warehouse reporting, retries, audit logging, and least-privilege access.

output_examples.input: Request: Plan secure authentication for a Benchling script.
output_examples.output: A concise setup plan covering environment variables, API key rotation, least-privilege access, and a users/me validation check.

output_examples.input: Request: Automate sample movement and documentation.
output_examples.output: A workflow outline that transfers containers, updates workflow tasks, creates an ELN entry, and links related entities.

output_examples.input: Request: Troubleshoot failed Benchling API calls.
output_examples.output: A checklist for status codes, credential format, tenant URL, permissions, pagination, rate limits, and retry behavior.

best_practices: Store credentials in environment variables or a secret manager.
Use server-side filters and pagination for large Benchling datasets.
Grant least-privilege access and review audit logs for integrations.
anti_patterns: Do not paste real API keys into prompts, source files, or examples.
Do not bulk update registry data without testing on a safe subset.
Do not load entire tenant datasets when API filters can narrow results.

faq.question: Does this skill connect to Benchling automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. You must provide credentials and execute any integration yourself.

faq.question: Which Benchling areas does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers registry entities, inventory, ELN entries, workflows, REST endpoints, events, and Data Warehouse concepts.

faq.question: Can I use OAuth instead of API keys?
faq.answer: Yes. The references explain OAuth client credentials and OIDC patterns for production and enterprise use cases.

faq.question: Does it include real credentials?
faq.answer: No. The examples use placeholders and recommend secure credential storage.

faq.question: Can it help with large exports?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes pagination, server-side filters, Data Warehouse access, and export planning.

faq.question: Is it specific to one Benchling tenant?
faq.answer: No. You must adapt tenant URLs, schema IDs, folder IDs, and permissions to your environment.
